physical_state_in: Soil + water + sunlight + olive tree stock
primary_transformation: Biological growth cycle: pruning + irrigation + integrated pest management + soil management
typical_time_scale: Perennial (1 year crop cycle; tree productive life 100-300 years)
D_parameters: Climate stress (drought/heat); fragmented land tenure (380K farms avg 7ha); CAP compliance; labor availability; water rights; alternate bearing cycle
C_parameters: Cooperative model (Dcoop/Hojiblanca); drip irrigation; PDO-certified varieties; advanced agronomic engineering; 340M tree heritage stock
notes: Spain 2.5M ha; 340M trees; 75% in Andalusia. Drought reduced 2022-23 harvest by 48%. CAP provides ~30% of eligible producer income. Traditional vs intensive grove duality (42% with <140 trees/ha; 3% super-intensive >400 trees/ha). Sources: oliveoilsfromspain.org; CaixaBank Research 2022; CDE/Univ Bern blog; Business Insider/Dcoop 2023.

primary_transformation: Mechanical vibration (vibradoras) + net collection + transport to mill. Timing critical: Nov-Jan optimum. Early harvest yields higher quality oil.
measurable_output: Tonnes of olives harvested per day per grove
D_parameters: Seasonal time window (3 months); weather dependency; labor shortage (15% seasonal worker deficit in 2023); drought reduces fruit attachment force; machinery investment cost
data_status: 000 families in largest cooperative; mechanization replaces hand-harvesting; yield benchmarks (Benito: 8
column17: 1700+ mills handle inflow. World largest mill at Villacarrillo (Jaen) processes 2500 tonnes olives/day. Dcoop: 75K families. Harvest season Nov-Jan. In 2023 seasonal worker shortage 15% (Spanish Ministry of Agriculture). Sources: Business Insider/Dcoop 2023; oliveoilsfromspain.org; Olive Oil Times export data.

physical_state_out: Crude olive oil (extra virgin / virgin / lampante) + alperujo (wet olive paste)
primary_transformation: Cold mechanical extraction: washing + crushing to paste + malaxation + centrifugal decanting. No heat or solvents in EVOO process.
typical_time_scale: 12-24 hours per batch (time-sensitive: oil quality degrades rapidly if olives stored)
measurable_output: Litres of olive oil extracted per tonne of olives
D_parameters: Quality grading (IOC acidity thresholds); energy intensity (decanters); fast-turnaround requirement (olives degrade within hours); EU quality standards; IOC certification
C_parameters: Cold extraction technology; Acesur AI Easy Taste quality analyzer (600 samples/day); 1700+ mills with capacity to handle peak harvest flow; Dcoop world largest storage 300K MT; PEF (Pulsed Electric Field) extraction technology at Acesur
notes: ~20% oil extraction rate from olives (varies by variety and ripeness). Extra virgin: <=0.8% acidity. Spain has 1700+ mills including world's largest at Villacarrillo (2500t/day). Acesur (La Espanola brand) uses AI-powered organoleptic analysis (Easy Taste). Solar-powered mills at Acesur. Sources: Deutsche Bank/Acesur 2025; Business Insider/Dcoop 2023; IOC definitions; foodswinesfromspain.com.

physical_state_in: Alperujo (wet olive paste byproduct from milling)
physical_state_out: Pomace oil (crude) + compost/fertilizer + biomass fuel pellets
primary_transformation: Solvent extraction of residual oil from alperujo; composting of dry pulp; biomass conversion for energy generation
measurable_output: Tonnes of pomace oil extracted; MWh of biomass energy generated
D_parameters: Solvent extraction regulatory compliance; separate pomace oil industry governance (Spain Professional Organization of Olive Pomace Oil recognized 2016); different quality and market positioning from virgin oils
C_parameters: Circular economy integration: alperujo as fertilizer/biomass for energy/animal feed/compost; pomace oil for food processing and cosmetics; Spain world leader in pomace oil production
notes: Alperujo is the main byproduct (olive waste): wet paste ~0.8t per tonne of olives processed. Used as: compost/fertilizer (soil amendment); biomass energy (heating mills); animal feed additive; crude pomace oil via solvent extraction. Spain has dedicated Professional Organization of Olive Pomace Oil. Sources: Olive Oil Times pomace 2016; Business Insider/Dcoop 2023 (alperujo composted for fertilizer or biomass fuel).

physical_state_out: Stable bottled or bulk olive oil ready for bottling/export
primary_transformation: Temperature-controlled inert storage in large stainless steel tanks (nitrogen-blanketed to prevent oxidation). Oil segregated by quality grade and harvest lot.
typical_time_scale: Months to up to 2 years (oil maintains quality under proper storage)
measurable_output: Tonnes of oil in storage; nitrogen consumption per tonne stored
output_unit: t stored / Nm3 N2 per t
D_parameters: Temperature regulation cost; nitrogen supply; tank maintenance; oil segregation and traceability; fire/explosion risk from oil vapors; tank capacity constraints at peak harvest
C_parameters: World's largest olive oil storage facility (Dcoop: 300K metric tonnes capacity at Antequera); nitrogen blanketing technology; stainless steel tanks; quality preservation for up to 2 years; detailed lot tracking
notes: Dcoop maintains the world's largest olive oil storage facility: 300,000 metric tonnes capacity at Antequera (equivalent to 1/3 of an oil tanker). Tanks are stainless steel, kept in darkness at constant temperature, nitrogen-blanketed. Oil can be stored up to 2 years. Sources: Business Insider/Dcoop 2023; oliveoilsfromspain.org.

physical_state_out: Bottled olive oil (glass/PET/metal) ready for retail or export
primary_transformation: Filtration + blending + filling + sealing + labeling. Both domestic brands (La Espanola/Atasur) and Italian bulk buyers (Salov/Filippo Berio) receive product.
measurable_output: Litres bottled per day; share bottled vs bulk exported
D_parameters: BOTTLENECK: ~67% of Spanish exports leave as bulk (EUR 3.22/kg avg) vs Italian rebranded at EUR 4.42/kg (EUR 1.20/kg premium gap); fragmented 1500 bottlers; glass cost increase +25% globally; PDO label complexity; lack of coordinated brand strategy; retail price pressure (Tesco own-brand EUR 3.95/L suppressing margins)
C_parameters: 1500+ bottlers; La Espanola (Acesur) and Atasur as Spanish premium brands; PDO/PGI certification framework; recent EU traceability standards (Royal Decree 760/2021); new quality standard requiring computerized bulk oil movement tracking since Oct 2021
notes: STRUCTURAL BOTTLENECK: Spain is world's largest producer but captures only EUR 3.22/kg average export price vs Italy's EUR 4.42/kg because ~67% of exports are bulk. Salov/Filippo Berio and other Italian companies blend and rebrand Spanish bulk oil under Italian-sounding names. This is Spain's primary value chain failure. Sources: CaixaBank Research 2022; Sustainable Food Trust 2018; CIHEAM/New Medit 2025; CDE/Univ Bern.

physical_state_in: Bottled or bulk olive oil (Spain warehouses)
physical_state_out: Olive oil delivered to international buyers (Italy bulk; USA/UK/Germany bottled)
primary_transformation: Road + short-sea shipping (MSC flexibags for bulk; refrigerated containers for bottled). Intermodal in Italy (Rubino RS road+rail). Specialist liquid logistics.
typical_time_scale: Days to weeks (Mediterranean bulk shipping 24-48h; transoceanic 3-6 weeks)
measurable_output: Tonnes shipped per mode; cost per tonne; transit time
D_parameters: Red Sea disruptions +10-15 days to Asia (late 2024); container rate inflation (2-3x pre-pandemic levels); glass fragility; specialized flexibag containers required; temperature sensitivity; complex customs and tariff framework
C_parameters: MSC Liquid Cargo Solutions (flexibag 24,000L per 20ft container); Rubino RS intermodal tank containers (ISO 9001/14001/GMP+); short-sea Spain-Italy corridor; global MSC network 120+ destinations; specialized door-to-door liquid logistics
notes: Key bulk logistics operators: MSC Spain (flexibag 24,000L per 20ft container); Rubino RS (Puglia Italy: 80+ year family company, bimodal tank containers, road+rail intermodal, ISO certified). Italy top destination 28.2%. USA now >EUR 1B exports. Short-sea shipping Spain-Italy primary bulk route. Sources: MSC Spain; Rubino RS; Olive Oil Times 2024.

physical_state_in: Delivered olive oil (bulk or bottled) at destination
physical_state_out: Final sold product at retail or foodservice; price captured by brand owner
primary_transformation: Brand positioning + retail shelf placement + PDO/PGI marketing + consumer conversion. Italian brands dominate premium shelves despite Spanish origin oil.
measurable_output: EUR per kg realized at retail vs farmgate; market share by brand
D_parameters: Italian brand premium capture (Filippo Berio/Salov/Bertolli); historical fraud (extra virgin mislabeling); oligopoly retail (Tesco/Carrefour/REWE hold >50% shelf); US tariffs (25% Oct 2019 to June 2021); EU CBAM emerging costs; retail pricing suppressing producer margins (CaixaBank: retail price does not reflect true production cost)
C_parameters: Growing consumer demand globally (EIT Food 2024: 61% EU consumers willing to pay 15%+ premium for organic); expanding USA/Asia/Germany markets; Spanish premium brands (La Espanola at 120 countries); PDO designations gaining recognition; IOC global quality standards; record EUR 6B export revenues 2023/24
notes: Trade opacity: Italian brands (Filippo Berio/Salov; Bertolli/Deoleo; Monini) package Spanish bulk oil under Italian-sounding names -- noted only in small print. Spain's export reached record EUR 6.04B in 2023/24 at EUR 8/kg average (vs EUR 3.22/kg two years prior -- reflects price spike not brand premium). USA market >EUR 1B in 2023/24 for first time. EVOO 69% of Spain's export volume. Sources: CaixaBank Research 2022; Sustainable Food Trust 2018; Olive Oil Times 2024; Persistence Market Research 2026.
